blocks.text: In a Yy pea plant the dominant allele Y is fully expressed and the recessive allele y not at all, so no intermediate (green) trait appears in Yy. This is complete dominance.

When scientists tested Mendel's ideas they found that results were not always the same. Many traits do not show complete dominance, and some traits are controlled by more than two alleles. The next topics cover incomplete dominance, co-dominance and multiple alleles.

blocks.explanation: The dominant allele is fully expressed in the heterozygote and the recessive one not at all, so the heterozygote looks like the dominant homozygote (Yy is yellow).

items: Complete dominance: Yy looks like YY.
Exceptions: incomplete dominance, co-dominance, multiple alleles.
